newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London gain on weak U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London gain on weak U.S. data.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied in London on Tuesday as market-makers marked share prices higher following weaker than expected U.S. employment cost and durable goods data, dealers said.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index closed up 216.82 points at 12,817.24 near the top of the day, after the Hang Seng Index closed down 9.75 points at 12,600.42 in Hong Kong.

Dealers said shares in banks and property stocks featured in the rally after the U.S. Employment Cost Index showed a rise of 0.6 per cent compared with forecasts around 0.9 per cent and March durable goods orders fell by an unexpected 3.0 per cent, compared with forecasts of being unchanged.
In the banks sector, shares in HSBC Holdings jumped HK$4.603 to HK$193.95, while New World Development lead the property stocks with a rise of HK$1.05 to HK$43.60.
Dealers said volume was light and the rally more closely reflected a mark-up of share prices by market-makers as opposed to genuine buying by investors.
-- Andrew Langlands, London Newsroom +44 171 542 3496 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
